rules.title: Prevailing party gets attorney's fees in pool contract disputes
rules.plain_english: In any lawsuit between an owner who contracted for swimming pool construction and the pool contractor over that contract, the court must award reasonable attorney's fees to whichever side wins.

parameters.trigger: action arising out of a contract for swimming pool construction
parties: person contracting for construction of a swimming pool

rules.applies_to: Swimming pool contractors (C-53 or B) and owners who contract for pool construction
rules.verbatim_quote: In any action between a person contracting for construction of a swimming pool and a swimming pool contractor arising out of a contract for swimming pool construction, the court shall award reasonable attorney’s fees to the prevailing party.
rules.effective: Added Stats 1979 ch 747 as 7169; renumbered Stats 1991 ch 1160 (no effective date printed)
rules.notes: Fee shifting is two-way (owner or contractor). Useful for a dispute-risk warning on pool contracts. Page 430 overlaps the previous chunk.

rules.title: Give CSLB solar disclosure document before sale, financing or lease
rules.plain_english: A solar energy system company must give the consumer CSLB's Solar Energy System Disclosure Document before completing a sale, financing, or lease of a residential solar energy system. CSLB (with the CPUC) publishes the form on its website.

parameters.document: Solar Energy System Disclosure Document (CSLB + CPUC, posted on CSLB website)
parameters.timing: prior to completion of a sale, financing, or lease of a solar energy system

rules.applies_to: Solar energy system companies/contractors selling, financing or leasing residential solar energy systems (1 kW to 5 MW AC)
rules.verbatim_quote: that a solar energy system company shall provide to a consumer prior to completion of a sale, financing, or lease of a solar energy system.
rules.notes: Does not apply to systems installed as a standard feature on new construction (7169(h)). See solar-energy-system-definition-threshold for scope.

rules.title: Solar disclosure on contract front page in 16-point bold
rules.plain_english: The solar disclosure document must be printed on the front page or cover page of every solar energy contract, in boldface 16-point type.

parameters.placement: front page or cover page of every solar energy contract

rules.applies_to: Every residential solar energy contract (sale, financing, lease)
rules.verbatim_quote: The “solar energy system disclosure document” shall be printed on the front page or cover page of every solar energy contract. The “solar energy system disclosure document” shall be printed in boldface 16-point type
rules.notes: Statute says 16-point (not 'at least'); a document generator should use exactly 16-pt bold or larger only if CSLB form permits.

verification.checked_against: 2026 CSLB Law Book (sources/lawbook.txt), PDF page 430 (B&P 7169(b))

rules.title: Solar disclosure must show total cost, complaint info, cancellation right
rules.plain_english: The front-page solar disclosure must include: (1) total cost and payments for the system including financing costs, (2) how and to whom the customer can complain, and (3) the consumer's cancellation right under B&P 7159.

required_primary_items: total cost and payments for the system, including financing costs
information on how and to whom customers may provide complaints
consumer's right to the applicable cancellation period pursuant to B&P 7159

rules.verbatim_quote: (1) The total cost and payments for the system, including financing costs. (2) Information on how and to whom customers may provide complaints. (3) The consumer’s right to the applicable cancellation period pursuant to Section 7159 of the Business and Professions Code.
rules.notes: The cancellation period length is set in B&P 7159 (not in this chunk).

verification.checked_against: 2026 CSLB Law Book (sources/lawbook.txt), PDF page 430 (B&P 7169(b)(1)-(3))

rules.title: Optional supporting pages of the solar disclosure
rules.plain_english: After the front page, CSLB's solar disclosure may include supporting information such as financing amounts and sources, panel-count and energy-production calculations, extra utility/monitoring fees, guaranteed rebate terms, final price without rebates, the company's contractor license number, lease vs. purchase differences, effects on home sale, and a performance calculator. A sales system should be able to supply these figures.

parameters.included_at: board's discretion, following the front/cover page
possible_items: amounts and sources of financing obtained
calculations used by the home improvement salesperson to determine number of panels needed
calculations used to determine how much energy the panels will generate
additional monthly electric company fees, turn-on charges, and internet monitoring fees for panels or inverters
terms and conditions of any guaranteed rebate
final contract price, without the inclusion of possible rebates
solar energy system company's contractor's license number
impacts of installations not performed to code
types of solar energy system malfunctions
difference between a solar lease and a solar purchase
impacts of financing/lease/contract terms on sale of the home, including balloon payments or system relocation if contract not assigned to new owner
calculator of projected system output, which may include an expected performance-based buy-down calculator

rules.verbatim_quote: (6) The final contract price, without the inclusion of possible rebates. (7) The solar energy system company’s contractor’s license number.
rules.notes: Whether these items are required depends on the current CSLB-published disclosure form; the statute makes them discretionary for the board.

rules.title: Solar contract and disclosure in the language of the sales pitch
rules.plain_english: The solar contract (sale, financing, or lease) and the disclosure document must be written in the same language that was principally used in the oral sales presentation or in the printed/digital marketing given to the consumer.

parameters.language_rule: same language principally used in oral sales presentation or print/digital marketing material given to consumer

rules.verbatim_quote: A contract for sale, financing, or lease of a solar energy system and the solar energy system disclosure document shall be written in the same language as was principally used in the oral sales presentation made to the consumer or the print or digital marketing material given to the consumer.
rules.notes: A CRM can capture the sales language and select the contract template accordingly.

verification.checked_against: 2026 CSLB Law Book (sources/lawbook.txt), PDF page 431 (B&P 7169(d))

rules.title: PACE form covers financing contract only, not installation contract
rules.plain_english: If the solar system uses PACE financing, the PACE Financing Estimate and Disclosure form (Streets & Highways Code 5898.17(b)) satisfies the disclosure requirement for the financing contract only; the installation contract still needs the CSLB solar disclosure.

parameters.trigger: Property Assessed Clean Energy (PACE) financing used
parameters.does_not_satisfy_for: underlying contract for installation of the solar energy system
parameters.form: Financing Estimate and Disclosure form, Streets & Highways Code 5898.17(b)

rules.applies_to: Residential solar projects financed through PACE
rules.verbatim_quote: the Financing Estimate and Disclosure form required by subdivision (b) of Section 5898.17 of the Streets and Highways Code shall satisfy the requirements of this section with respect to the financing contract only, but not, however, with respect to the underlying contract for installation of the solar energy system.
rules.notes: CSLB posts the PACE form on its website (7169(f)).

rules.title: Solar disclosure scope: residential, 1 kW to 5 MW AC
rules.plain_english: For the solar disclosure law, a 'solar energy system' is a device installed on a residential building, mainly to generate electricity, producing at least 1 kW and no more than 5 MW AC rated peak, and meeting Public Resources Code 25782 eligibility criteria.

parameters.primary_purpose: collection and distribution of solar energy for generation of electricity
parameters.eligibility: meets or exceeds criteria under Public Resources Code 25782

rules.applies_to: Determining whether B&P 7169 disclosure rules apply to a solar project
rules.verbatim_quote: “solar energy system” means a solar energy device to be installed on a residential building that has the primary purpose of providing for the collection and distribution of solar energy for the generation of electricity, that produces at least one kW, and not more than five MW, alternating current rated peak electricity
rules.notes: Systems under 1 kW AC, over 5 MW AC, or on non-residential buildings fall outside this definition.

verification.checked_against: 2026 CSLB Law Book (sources/lawbook.txt), PDF pages 431-432 (B&P 7169(g))

rules.title: Solar disclosure not required for standard-feature new construction
rules.plain_english: The solar disclosure rules do not apply when the solar system is installed as a standard feature on new construction.

parameters.exempt_if: solar energy system installed as a standard feature on new construction

rules.applies_to: Builders/developers including solar as a standard feature of new homes
rules.verbatim_quote: This section does not apply to a solar energy system that is installed as a standard feature on new construction.
rules.notes: An optional upgrade sold to a new-home buyer may not be a 'standard feature'; not addressed in text.

rules.title: CSLB publishes annual solar complaint report
rules.plain_english: CSLB takes consumer complaints and questions about solar companies and solar contractors (including complaints from other state agencies) and, starting July 1, 2019, publishes an annual report on its and the CPUC's websites listing complaint numbers and types, the ZIP code where each originated, and the disposition of every complaint against a solar contractor.

report_contents: ZIP Code where consumer complaint originated
disposition of all complaints received against a solar contractor

rules.applies_to: Solar energy system companies and solar contractors (reputation/complaint exposure)
rules.verbatim_quote: Beginning on July 1, 2019, the board annually shall compile a report documenting consumer complaints relating to solar contractors. The report shall be made available publicly on the board’s and the Public Utilities Commission’s internet websites.
rules.notes: Board-administration duty, included because complaint dispositions against solar contractors become public.

rules.title: Asbestos consultants and site surveillance technicians need DOSH certification
rules.plain_english: Since July 1, 1992, nobody may work as an asbestos consultant or site surveillance technician unless certified by Cal/OSHA's Division of Occupational Safety and Health (DOSH).

parameters.certifying_agency: Division of Occupational Safety and Health (DOSH)

rules.applies_to: Persons providing asbestos consulting/monitoring services on projects with 100+ sq ft of asbestos-containing material
rules.verbatim_quote: No person shall, on or after July 1, 1992, engage in the practice of an asbestos consultant as defined in Section 7181, or as a site surveillance technician as defined in Section 7182, unless he or she is certified by the Division of Occupational Safety and Health
rules.notes: Article 11 applies only to asbestos abatement projects involving 100 sq ft or more of ACM surface area (7189.5).

rules.title: Contractor may take up to 12 asbestos bulk samples without consultant certification
rules.plain_english: A licensed contractor or registered asbestos abatement contractor does not need asbestos consultant certification to take no more than 12 bulk samples of suspected asbestos material that will be removed, repaired or disturbed on a residential construction project, but only for bid preparation, checking its own employees' exposure, or confirming an abatement contract was completed. The person sampling must be an AHERA-certified building inspector.

parameters.setting: construction project in a residential dwelling
parameters.material: suspected asbestos-containing material required to be removed, repaired, or disturbed
permitted_purposes: evaluating exposure to its own employees during construction or asbestos abatement
determining for its own purposes or for communicating whether an asbestos abatement contract has been satisfactorily completed
parameters.sampler_qualification: certified building inspector under AHERA, 40 CFR 763, appendix C to subpart E

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors and registered asbestos abatement contractors on residential projects
rules.verbatim_quote: Certification as an asbestos consultant or site surveillance technician shall not be required when a licensed contractor or registered asbestos abatement contractor takes no more than 12 bulk samples of suspected asbestos-containing material that is required to be removed, repaired, or disturbed as part of a construction project in a residential dwelling
rules.effective: Added Stats 1990 ch 1255; amended Stats 1996 ch 526 (no effective date printed)
rules.notes: Text does not state the consequence beyond 12 samples; by implication the exemption is lost and consultant certification rules apply. The same 12-sample exemption also applies to the 7187 conflict-of-interest rule.

rules.title: Contractors may not do asbestos risk assessment or clearance air monitoring
rules.plain_english: A licensed contractor or asbestos abatement contractor may not provide professional asbestos health and safety services, perform asbestos risk assessments, or (unless another law allows) perform clearance air monitoring after abatement. Those are consultant functions.

prohibited_activities: clearance air monitoring following asbestos abatement, unless otherwise permitted by law

rules.applies_to: All licensed contractors and asbestos abatement contractors
rules.source_location: 2026 CSLB Law Book, PDF pages 433 and 437
rules.verbatim_quote: No licensed contractor or asbestos abatement contractor may provide professional health and safety services or perform any asbestos risk assessment. ... nor does it permit a licensed contractor or asbestos abatement contractor to perform clearance air monitoring following asbestos abatement, unless otherwise permitted by law.
rules.effective: Added Stats 1990 ch 1255; amended Stats 1996 ch 526 (no effective date printed)
rules.notes: Clearance air monitoring must be done by an independent certified asbestos consultant/technician.

rules.title: Asbestos bid may report sampling results; contractor may charge for bid prep
rules.plain_english: An asbestos abatement bid may state the results and locations of asbestos sampling and how the asbestos will be abated, and the contractor may charge for bid preparation, including lab analysis costs.

bid_may_include: how the asbestos will be abated
parameters.may_charge_for: bid preparation, including cost of laboratory analysis of asbestos-containing material

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors and asbestos abatement contractors bidding abatement work
rules.source_location: 2026 CSLB Law Book, PDF pages 433 and 437
rules.verbatim_quote: A bid for asbestos abatement may communicate the results and location of sampling for the presence of asbestos and how the asbestos will be abated. ... A licensed contractor or asbestos abatement contractor may seek compensation for bid preparation, including the cost of laboratory analysis of asbestos-containing material.
rules.effective: Added Stats 1990 ch 1255; amended Stats 1996 ch 526 (no effective date printed)
rules.notes: Bid template field: sampling results, sample locations, abatement method; optional bid-prep/lab fee line item.

rules.title: Building owner must hire DOSH-certified asbestos consultant
rules.plain_english: When a building owner or operator hires someone for asbestos consulting or site surveillance technician work, the owner must contract with a DOSH-certified person.

parameters.trigger: engaging asbestos consulting or site surveillance technician services (B&P 7181/7182) after 1992-07-01
parameters.must_hire: person certified by DOSH under Labor Code 9021.5(b) regulations

rules.applies_to: Building owners/operators (project owners) on asbestos projects
rules.verbatim_quote: When a building owner or operator engages the services of a person to perform asbestos consulting or site surveillance technician activities as defined in Sections 7181 and 7182 after July 1, 1992, the building owner or operator shall contract with a person who is certified by the Division of Occupational Safety and Health
rules.notes: Owner-side compliance check: verify consultant's DOSH certification card before contracting.

rules.title: Definition: asbestos consultant
rules.plain_english: An asbestos consultant is anyone who contracts to provide professional health and safety services for asbestos-containing material, including building inspections, abatement design, contract administration, supervising site surveillance technicians, sampling, asbestos management plans and clearance air monitoring.
rules.applies_to: Classifying asbestos-related service roles on a project
rules.verbatim_quote: An “asbestos consultant,” as used in this chapter, means any person who contracts to provide professional health and safety services relating to asbestos-containing material ... including building inspections, abatement project design, contract administration, supervision of site surveillance technicians
rules.effective: Added Stats 1990 ch 1255 (no effective date printed)

rules.title: Definition: site surveillance technician
rules.plain_english: A site surveillance technician is an independent on-site representative of an asbestos consultant who monitors others' abatement work, does area and personnel air monitoring, and performs building surveys and contract administration at the consultant's direction.

parameters.role: independent onsite representative of an asbestos consultant
duties: monitors asbestos abatement activities of others
asbestos air monitoring for area and personnel samples
building surveys and contract administration at direction of an asbestos consultant

rules.applies_to: Classifying asbestos-related service roles on a project
rules.verbatim_quote: A “site surveillance technician” means any person who acts as an independent onsite representative of an asbestos consultant who monitors the asbestos abatement activities of others, provides asbestos air monitoring services for area and personnel samples, and performs building surveys and contract administration at the direction of an asbestos consultant.
rules.effective: Added Stats 1990 ch 1255 (no effective date printed)

rules.title: DOSH asbestos certification: 15-day completeness notice, 45-day issuance
rules.plain_english: DOSH must tell an asbestos consultant/technician applicant within 15 days of receipt whether the application is complete or deficient, and must issue the certification card within 45 days after a complete application is filed. If it misses these deadlines, it must issue a provisional card.

parameters.issue_card_from: date of filing of completed application
parameters.if_deadline_missed: provisional certification card issued until procedures completed

rules.applies_to: Applicants for DOSH asbestos consultant / site surveillance technician certification
rules.verbatim_quote: Within 15 days of receipt of an application for certification pursuant to this article, the division shall inform the applicant in writing either (1) that the application is complete and accepted, or (2) that it is deficient ... Within 45 days of the date of filing of a completed application, the division shall issue
rules.effective: Added Stats 1990 ch 1255 (no effective date printed)
rules.notes: Agency deadline; useful for scheduling when a company's staff must get certified before a project.

verification.checked_against: 2026 CSLB Law Book (sources/lawbook.txt), PDF page 434 (B&P 7183(a))

rules.title: DOSH must revoke asbestos certification for fraud or gross/repeated negligence
rules.plain_english: DOSH must revoke an asbestos consultant's or technician's certification if it was obtained under false pretenses, or if the holder acted with gross negligence or fraud, or committed repeated negligent acts (after an Administrative Procedure Act hearing).

parameters.procedure: Government Code 11500 et seq. (Administrative Procedure Act)

rules.applies_to: DOSH-certified asbestos consultants and site surveillance technicians
rules.verbatim_quote: In the event the division determines that a certified asbestos consultant or site surveillance technician obtained certification under false pretenses, or that a certified asbestos consultant or site surveillance technician acted in a grossly negligent or fraudulent manner, or engaged in repeated acts of negligence, the division shall revoke that person’s certification.
rules.effective: Added Stats 1990 ch 1255 (no effective date printed)

verification.checked_against: 2026 CSLB Law Book (sources/lawbook.txt), PDF page 434 (B&P 7183.5)

rules.title: Asbestos consultant qualification: experience/education ladder + AHERA + exam
rules.plain_english: To be a certified asbestos consultant you need one of: 1 year asbestos experience + BS in engineering/architecture/industrial hygiene/construction management/related science; 2 years + any bachelor's; 3 years + related AA; or 4 years + high school diploma. You also need a valid federal AHERA certificate for the work type and must pass a DOSH exam.

experience_education_options.education: bachelor of science in engineering, architecture, industrial hygiene, construction management, or related biological or physical science
associate of arts in engineering, architecture, industrial hygiene, construction management, or related biological or physical science

also_required: valid federal AHERA certificate (15 USC 2641 et seq.) for the type of work, or DOSH-determined equivalent
passing score on DOSH-approved or DOSH-administered examination
exam_subjects: OSHA, DOSH, EPA, air district and DHS regulatory requirements
state-of-the-art abatement and control work procedures
AHERA training for inspectors, management planners, supervisors
industrial hygiene sampling methodology and recordkeeping

rules.verbatim_quote: (1) One year of asbestos-related experience, and a bachelor of science degree in engineering, architecture, industrial hygiene, construction management, or a related biological or physical science. (2) Two years of asbestos-related experience, and a bachelor’s degree.
rules.effective: Added Stats 1990 ch 1255 (no effective date printed)

rules.title: Site surveillance technician qualification: 6 months + HS + AHERA + exam
rules.plain_english: A certified site surveillance technician needs 6 months of asbestos experience under an asbestos consultant's supervision, a high school diploma or equivalent, a valid AHERA certificate, and a passing DOSH exam score.

parameters.experience_condition: under the supervision of an asbestos consultant
parameters.federal_certificate: valid AHERA certificate for type of work, or equivalent
parameters.exam: passing score on DOSH-approved/administered exam (5 subject areas)

rules.applies_to: Individuals seeking site surveillance technician certification
rules.verbatim_quote: (a) Having six months of asbestos-related experience under the supervision of an asbestos consultant. (b) Possession of a high school diploma or equivalent.
rules.effective: Added Stats 1990 ch 1255 (no effective date printed)

rules.title: Owner's asbestos consultant cannot have an interest in the abatement contractor
rules.plain_english: When a building owner hires an asbestos consultant or site surveillance technician, that consultant may not have any financial or ownership interest in the asbestos abatement contractor hired for the same project. A contractor may still hire its own consultant for its workers' health and safety.

parameters.trigger: building owner or operator contracts with asbestos consultant or site surveillance technician
parameters.prohibited: consultant/technician has any financial or proprietary interest in an asbestos abatement contractor hired for the same project
parameters.exception_contractor_hire: contractor may hire a consultant to provide health and safety services for the contractor's personnel
parameters.exception_bulk_samples: does not apply to contractor taking <= 12 bulk samples in residential dwelling for the listed purposes

rules.applies_to: Building owners, asbestos consultants/technicians, and asbestos abatement contractors on the same project
rules.verbatim_quote: that asbestos consultant or site surveillance technician shall not have any financial or proprietary interest in an asbestos abatement contractor hired for the same project. However, this section shall not preclude the hiring of a consultant by a contractor for the purpose of providing health and safety services for the personnel of the contractor.
rules.effective: Added Stats 1990 ch 1255; amended Stats 1996 ch 526 (no effective date printed)
rules.notes: Legislative intent: consultant work (clearance air monitoring, design, contract administration) must reflect independent professional judgment.

rules.title: Penalties: uncertified asbestos consulting or conflict of interest
rules.plain_english: Practicing as an asbestos consultant or site surveillance technician without certification, or violating the conflict-of-interest rule, is an infraction on a first conviction ($1,000-$3,000 fine). A later conviction is a misdemeanor: certification must be revoked or suspended, and the fine is $3,000-$5,000 and/or up to one year in county jail.

violations: practicing as asbestos consultant or site surveillance technician without DOSH certification

rules.title: Asbestos consultant rules apply at 100+ sq ft of ACM
rules.plain_english: The asbestos consultant certification article applies to asbestos abatement projects involving 100 square feet or more of asbestos-containing material surface area.
rules.verbatim_quote: This article shall apply to asbestos abatement projects within the meaning of asbestos-related work as defined in Section 6501.8 of the Labor Code, and which involves 100 square feet or more of surface area of asbestos containing material.
rules.effective: Added Stats 1990 ch 1255 (no effective date printed)
rules.notes: Below 100 sq ft, Article 11 (B&P 7180-7189.7) does not apply; other Cal/OSHA asbestos rules may still apply.

rules.title: State agencies may use their own DOSH-certified staff as asbestos consultants
rules.plain_english: State agencies need not hire outside asbestos consultants if their own assigned employees are DOSH-certified; where feasible, the state should use associate or senior industrial hygienists. Attorneys giving asbestos legal advice to owners need not be certified.

parameters.condition: state employees performing B&P 7181/7182 activities must be DOSH-certified
parameters.attorney_exemption: attorneys providing asbestos legal advice to building owners/operators need not be certified (7189.7(b))

rules.applies_to: State agencies as owners of state-owned or leased buildings
rules.verbatim_quote: Nothing in this article shall be construed to require agencies of the state to contract with asbestos consultants or site surveillance technicians who are not employees of the state as long as employees of the state who are assigned to perform the activities described in Sections 7181 and 7182 have been certified by the division

rules.title: No public official's name in ads without written authorization
rules.plain_english: A licensed contractor may not use the name or position of a public official (local or state agency member, officer, employee, or consultant) in advertising or promotional material without that official's written authorization.

parameters.requires: written authorization of the public official
parameters.public_official_definition: member, officer, employee, or consultant of a local government agency (Gov Code 82041) or state agency (Gov Code 82049)

rules.verbatim_quote: The name or position of a public official may not be used in an advertisement or any promotional material by a person licensed under this chapter, without the written authorization of the public official.
rules.effective: Added Stats 1994 ch 1135 (no effective date printed)
rules.notes: Book cross-references Civil Code 1770 (Unfair Practices) in the Appendix.

rules.title: Required disclaimer when an authorized public official appears in ads
rules.plain_english: If a printed ad uses a public official's name or position with written authorization, it must include a disclaimer in at least 10-point roman boldface, in a contrasting color, set apart from other text, stating the official does not endorse the product/service in an official capacity. Broadcast ads must read the statement aloud clearly.

parameters.trigger: printed advertisement/promotional material uses public official's name or position with written authorization

rules.effective: Added Stats 1994 ch 1135 (no effective date printed)

rules.title: Residential (1-4 unit) arbitration clause must be titled ARBITRATION OF DISPUTES
rules.plain_english: If a contract for work on residential property with four or fewer units has an arbitration clause, it must be clearly titled 'ARBITRATION OF DISPUTES'. In a printed contract it must be in at least 10-point roman boldface, or contrasting red print in at least 8-point roman boldface; in a typed contract, in capital letters.

parameters.trigger: contract for work on residential property contains an arbitration provision between the principals
printed_contract_format_options: contrasting red print in at least 8-point roman boldface type

rules.applies_to: Contractors whose contracts for work on 1-4 unit residential property include arbitration
rules.verbatim_quote: If a contract for work on residential property with four or fewer units contains a provision for arbitration of a dispute between the principals in the transaction, the provision shall be clearly titled “ARBITRATION OF DISPUTES.”
rules.effective: Added Stats 1994 ch 1135 (no effective date printed)
rules.notes: Applies to any contract for work on such property (not only home improvement contracts).

verification.checked_against: 2026 CSLB Law Book (sources/lawbook.txt), PDF page 439 (B&P 7191(a))

rules.title: Mandatory arbitration NOTICE text and initial line
rules.plain_english: Right after the arbitration clause and immediately before the space where the parties initial agreement or refusal, the contract must print the statutory NOTICE (giving up court/jury trial, discovery and appeal rights) and the statement 'WE HAVE READ AND UNDERSTAND...'. Same formatting rules: 10-pt roman bold or red 8-pt roman bold if printed; capitals if typed.

parameters.placement: immediately following the arbitration provision and immediately before the line or space for parties to indicate assent or nonassent
parameters.notice_text: NOTICE: BY INITIALING IN THE SPACE BELOW YOU ARE AGREEING TO HAVE ANY DISPUTE ARISING OUT OF THE MATTERS INCLUDED IN THE ‘ARBITRATION OF DISPUTES’ PROVISION DECIDED BY NEUTRAL ARBITRATION AS PROVIDED BY CALIFORNIA LAW AND YOU ARE GIVING UP ANY RIGHTS YOU MIGHT POSSESS TO HAVE THE DISPUTE LITIGATED IN A COURT OR JURY TRIAL. BY INITIALING IN THE SPACE BELOW YOU ARE GIVING UP YOUR JUDICIAL RIGHTS TO DISCOVERY AND APPEAL, UNLESS THOSE RIGHTS ARE SPECIFICALLY INCLUDED IN THE ‘ARBITRATION OF DISPUTES’ PROVISION. rules.title: Definition: home inspection and home inspector
rules.plain_english: A home inspection is a noninvasive, physical, paid examination of the mechanical, electrical, plumbing, structural and essential components of a 1-4 unit residence done in connection with a property transfer, to find material defects. Any consultation called a home inspection (or similar) counts. A home inspector is anyone who performs one.

parameters.trigger: in connection with a transfer of real property (see 7195(e))
parameters.includes: any consultation represented to be a home inspection or any confusingly similar term
parameters.home_inspector: any individual who performs a home inspection

rules.applies_to: Contractors or firms offering pre-sale/transfer inspections of 1-4 unit homes
rules.verbatim_quote: “Home inspection” is a noninvasive, physical examination, performed for a fee in connection with a transfer, as defined in subdivision (e), of real property, of the mechanical, electrical, or plumbing systems or the structural and essential components of a residential dwelling of one to four units designed to identify material defects in those systems, structures, and components.
rules.notes: Chapter 9.3 does not create a CSLB license for home inspectors; it sets duties and unfair practices.

rules.title: Definition: transfer (triggers home inspection rules)
rules.plain_english: A 'transfer' means a sale, exchange, installment land sales contract, lease with option to purchase, any other option to purchase, or ground lease coupled with improvements, of real property or a residential stock cooperative with 1 to 4 dwelling units.

parameters.property: real property or residential stock cooperative

rules.verbatim_quote: “Transfer” is a transfer by sale, exchange, installment land sales contract, as defined in Section 2985 of the Civil Code, lease with an option to purchase, any other option to purchase, or ground lease coupled with improvements, of real property or residential stock cooperative, improved with or consisting of not less than one nor more than four dwelling units.

rules.title: Home inspection of pool/spa must report drowning prevention features
rules.plain_english: When a property with a pool or spa is transferred, the home inspection must check which of the seven drowning prevention safety features listed in Health & Safety Code 115922(a) are present, and the report must identify them and specifically state if the pool or spa has fewer than two.

parameters.trigger: transfer of real property with a swimming pool or spa
parameters.report_must_identify: which, if any, of the seven features the pool or spa is equipped with
parameters.flag_statement: report shall specifically state if the pool or spa has fewer than two listed features

rules.applies_to: Home inspectors (including contractors performing home inspections) on 1-4 unit homes with pools/spas
rules.verbatim_quote: In a dwelling with a pool or spa, the “home inspection report” shall identify which, if any, of the seven drowning prevention safety features listed in subdivision (a) of Section 115922 of the Health and Safety Code the pool or spa is equipped with and shall specifically state if the pool or spa has fewer than two of the listed drowning prevention safety features.
rules.notes: The seven features themselves are listed in H&S 115922(a), not in this chunk.

number of window glass panes and frame types
heating and cooling equipment and water heating systems
age and fuel type of major appliances
type of thermostat and other systems
general integrity and potential leakage areas of walls, window areas, doors, duct systems
solar control efficiency of existing windows

rules.title: Definition: material defect
rules.plain_english: A material defect is a condition that significantly affects the value, desirability, habitability or safety of the dwelling. Style or aesthetics do not make something defective.
rules.verbatim_quote: A “material defect” is a condition that significantly affects the value, desirability, habitability, or safety of the dwelling. Style or aesthetics shall not be considered in determining whether a system, structure, or component is defective.

rules.title: Home inspection report contents
rules.plain_english: A home inspection report is a written, paid report issued after the inspection that clearly describes the inspected systems, structures and components, any material defects found, and recommendations (including referrals for evaluation by appropriate persons).

must_include: description and identification of the inspected systems, structures, or components
recommendations regarding conditions observed or recommendations for evaluation by appropriate persons
pool/spa: drowning prevention features identified; statement if fewer than two

No watering-restriction penalty may be imposed for running the system for the inspection.

observation during operation (minutes specified in report) of spray to hardscape, surface runoff, ponding
notation whether inspection limited by snow, ice, or other site conditions

rules.title: Claimed experience must be documented; at least 3% field-investigated

rules.title: License experience: 4 years within the last 10 years in the class

A journeyman is a fully qualified worker who can work without supervision, or who completed an apprenticeship.

rules.title: CSLB processing deadlines: applications requiring exam

rules.applies_to: Applicants for original license, additional classification, or qualifier replacement with exam

rules.title: Licensees may not contract outside their classifications
rules.plain_english: Every license is classified as Class A (general engineering), Class B (general building), or a specialty (C) class. A contractor licensed in one classification may not contract in another classification's field unless also licensed in it or the work is incidental and supplemental (16 CCR 831).

parameters.rule: no contracting in field of another classification unless also licensed in it or permitted by 16 CCR 831

rules.verbatim_quote: (b) Contractors licensed in one classification shall be prohibited from contracting in the field of any other classification unless they are also licensed in that classification or are permitted to do so by Section 831.
rules.notes: Core check for bid/contract scope vs. license classes held.

rules.title: Incidental and supplemental work: essential to licensed work
rules.plain_english: Work in another classification is 'incidental and supplemental' to a specialty contractor's licensed work if it is essential to accomplish the licensed work. The specialty contractor may do it with its own employees or subcontract it.

parameters.test: work in other classification is essential to accomplish the work in which the contractor is classified

rules.verbatim_quote: For purposes of Section 7059, work in other classifications is “incidental and supplemental” to the work for which a specialty contractor is licensed if that work is essential to accomplish the work in which the contractor is classified. A specialty contractor may use subcontractors to complete the incidental and supplemental work, or they may use their own employees to do so.
rules.notes: Subcontracting incidental work still requires the sub to hold the proper class (general CSLB rules).

rules.title: List of CSLB specialty (C) classifications
rules.plain_english: CSLB specialty classes are: C-2 Insulation/Acoustical, C-4 Boiler/Hot Water/Steam, C-5 Framing/Rough Carpentry, C-6 Cabinet/Millwork/Finish Carpentry, C-7 Low Voltage, C-8 Concrete, C-9 Drywall, C-10 Electrical, C-11 Elevator, C-12 Earthwork/Paving, C-13 Fencing, C-15 Flooring, C-16 Fire Protection, C-17 Glazing, C-20 HVAC, C-21 Building Moving/Demolition, C-22 Asbestos Abatement, C-23 Ornamental Metal, C-27 Landscaping, C-28 Lock/Security, C-29 Masonry, C-31 Traffic Control, C-32 Parking/Highway Improvement, C-33 Painting, C-34 Pipeline, C-35 Lathing/Plastering, C-36 Plumbing, C-38 Refrigeration, C-39 Roofing, C-42 Sanitation, C-43 Sheet Metal, C-45 Sign, C-46 Solar, C-47 Manufactured Housing, C-49 Tree/Palm, C-50 Reinforcing Steel, C-51 Structural Steel, C-53 Swimming Pool, C-54 Tile, C-55 Water Conditioning, C-57 Well Drilling, C-60 Welding, C-61 Limited Specialty. Specialty contractors must work to the standards of their trade.

classes.C-4: Boiler, Hot Water Heating and Steam Fitting
classes.C-6: Cabinet, Mill Work and Finish Carpentry
classes.C-20: Warm-Air Heating, Ventilating and Air Conditioning

parameters.performance_standard: art, experience, science and skill necessary to satisfactorily organize, administer, construct and complete projects, in accordance with the standards of their trade

rules.verbatim_quote: Specialty contractors shall perform their trade using the art, experience, science and skill necessary to satisfactorily organize, administer, construct and complete projects under their classification, in accordance with the standards of their trade.
rules.notes: Class A and Class B are defined in B&P 7056/7057 (not in this chunk). C-61 has many CSLB-designated subcategories (D-codes) not listed here.

rules.title: C-2 Insulation and Acoustical scope
rules.plain_english: C-2 contractors install any insulating media and preformed architectural acoustical materials for temperature and/or sound control.
rules.verbatim_quote: An insulation and acoustical contractor installs any insulating media and preformed architectural acoustical materials for the purpose of temperature and/or sound control.

rules.title: C-4 Boiler, Hot-Water Heating and Steam Fitting scope
rules.plain_english: C-4 contractors install, service and repair power boilers, hot-water heating systems and steam fitting, including fire-tube and water-tube boilers, low-pressure hot-water boilers, piping, valves, gauges, pumps, radiators, convectors, fuel oil tanks/lines, chimneys, flues, heat insulation and associated equipment including solar heating equipment.

scope_includes: fire-tube and water-tube steel power boilers
solar heating equipment associated with these systems

rules.verbatim_quote: A boiler, hot-water heating and steam fitting contractor installs, services and repairs power boiler installations, hot-water heating systems and steam fitting ... and all other equipment, including solar heating equipment, associated with these systems.

rules.title: C-5 Framing and Rough Carpentry scope
rules.plain_english: C-5 contractors do form work, framing and rough carpentry for framed structures, including sub-flooring, siding, exterior staircases and railings, overhead doors, roof decking, truss members and sheathing.
rules.verbatim_quote: A framing and rough carpentry contractor performs any form work, framing or rough carpentry necessary to construct framed structures; installs or repairs individual components of framing systems and performs any rough carpentry or associated work

rules.title: C-6 Cabinet, Millwork and Finish Carpentry scope
rules.plain_english: C-6 contractors make cabinets, cases, sashes, doors, trims, nonbearing partitions and other finish carpentry from wood or other products, and place, erect and finish them in structures.

scope_includes: placing, erecting and finishing cabinets and millwork in structures

rules.verbatim_quote: A cabinet, millwork and finish carpentry contractor makes cabinets, cases, sashes, doors, trims, nonbearing partitions and other items of ... This contractor also places, erects, and finishes such cabinets and millwork in structures.

rules.title: C-7 Low Voltage Systems: energy-limited, max 91 volts, no fire alarms
rules.plain_english: C-7 contractors install, service and maintain energy-limited communication and low voltage systems not exceeding 91 volts (phone, sound, cable TV, CCTV, satellite dishes, instrumentation and temperature controls, low voltage landscape lighting). Low voltage fire alarm systems are excluded.
rules.verbatim_quote: A communication and low voltage contractor installs, services and maintains all types of communication and low voltage systems which are energy limited and do not exceed 91 volts. ... Low voltage fire alarm systems are specifically not included in this section.
rules.notes: Scope check: system voltage > 91 V or fire alarm requires another class (e.g., C-10).

verification.checked_against: 2026 CSLB Law Book (sources/lawbook.txt), PDF page 462 (16 CCR 832.07)

rules.title: C-8 Concrete scope
rules.plain_english: C-8 contractors form, pour, place, finish and install mass, pavement, flat and other concrete work and set screeds. The class does not cover contractors whose only business is plaster coatings or placing reinforcing steel.

scope_includes: forming, pouring, placing, finishing, installing mass, pavement, flat and other concrete work
placing and setting screeds for pavements or flatwork
scope_excludes: contractors whose sole business is application of plaster coatings
contractors whose sole business is placing/erecting reinforcing steel or bars

rules.verbatim_quote: A concrete contractor forms, pours, places, finishes and installs specified mass, pavement, flat and other concrete work; and places and sets screeds for pavements or flatwork.

rules.title: C-9 Drywall scope
rules.plain_english: C-9 contractors lay out and install gypsum wallboard and assemblies, including nonstructural metal framing, and do taping and texturing.
rules.verbatim_quote: A drywall contractor lays out and installs gypsum wall board and gypsum wallboard assemblies including nonstructural metal framing members, and performs the taping and texturing operations including the applications of compounds that adhere to wall board to produce a continuous smooth or textured surface.

rules.title: C-10 Electrical scope (includes batteries and PV; stayed amendment)
rules.plain_english: C-10 contractors place, install, erect or connect any electrical wires, fixtures, appliances, apparatus, raceways, conduits, battery energy storage systems, photovoltaic solar systems or parts thereof that generate, transmit, transform or use electricity.

rules.title: C-11 Elevator scope
rules.plain_english: C-11 contractors fabricate, erect, install and repair elevators, including sheave beams, motors, cables, guides, cabs, counterweights, doors (including sidewalk elevator doors), controls and signal systems for electric, hydraulic and manual elevators.
rules.verbatim_quote: An elevator contractor fabricates, erects, installs and repairs elevators, including sheave beams, motors, sheaves, cable and wire rope, guides, cab, counterweights, doors (including sidewalk elevator doors), automatic and manual controls, signal systems

rules.title: C-12 Earthwork and Paving scope
rules.plain_english: C-12 contractors dig, move and place earth materials for cuts, fills, excavations, grades, trenches, backfill and incidental tunnels (including use of explosives), and mix, fabricate and place paving and other surfacing.

scope_includes: use of explosives for these purposes
mixing, fabricating and placing paving and surfacing materials

rules.title: C-13 Fencing scope (excludes masonry walls)
rules.plain_english: C-13 contractors build and repair all types of fences, corrals, runs, railings, cribs, game court enclosures, guard rails and barriers, playground equipment, backstops, posts, flagpoles and gates, but not masonry walls.
rules.verbatim_quote: A fencing contractor constructs, erects, alters, or repairs all types of fences, corrals, runs, railings, cribs, game court enclosures, guard rails and barriers, playground game equipment, backstops, posts, flagpoles, and gates, excluding masonry walls.

rules.title: C-15 Flooring and Floor Covering scope (excludes ceramic tile)
rules.plain_english: C-15 contractors prepare surfaces and install carpet, resilient sheet and tile, wood floors (including finishing and repair) and other flooring materials, except ceramic tile.

rules.title: C-16 Fire Protection scope (excludes electrical alarms)
rules.plain_english: C-16 contractors lay out, fabricate and install all types of fire protection systems and associated equipment, excluding electrical alarm systems.

scope_includes: all types of fire protection systems

rules.verbatim_quote: A fire protection contractor lays out, fabricates and installs all types of fire protection systems; including all the equipment associated with these systems, excluding electrical alarm systems.

rules.title: C-17 Glazing scope
rules.plain_english: C-17 contractors select, cut, assemble and install all glass, mirrored glass and glass substitutes, and fabricate and glaze frames, panels, sashes and doors.

scope_includes: fabrication and glazing of frames, panels, sashes and doors

rules.verbatim_quote: A glazing contractor selects, cuts, assembles and/or installs all makes and kinds of glass, glass work, mirrored glass, and glass substitute materials for glazing; executes the fabrication and glazing of frames, panels, sashes and doors; and/or installs these items in any structure.

rules.title: C-20 Warm-Air Heating, Ventilating and Air-Conditioning scope
rules.plain_english: C-20 contractors fabricate, install, maintain, service and repair warm-air heating systems, water heating heat pumps, ventilating and air-conditioning systems with their ducts, registers, flues, controls and filters, including solar-powered HVAC.

rules.verbatim_quote: A warm-air heating, ventilating and air-conditioning contractor fabricates, installs, maintains, services and repairs warm-air heating systems and water heating heat pumps, complete with warm-air appliances

rules.title: C-21 Building Moving/Demolition scope
rules.plain_english: C-21 contractors raise, lower, crib, underpin, demolish, and move or remove structures and their foundations, but not alterations, additions, repairs or rehabilitation of the parts of a structure that stay.

rules.title: C-22 Asbestos Abatement scope; DOSH rules govern work and documents
rules.plain_english: C-22 contractors perform asbestos abatement (containment, encapsulation, removal and disposal of asbestos-containing construction materials) in and on buildings. asbestos abatement contractor licensed in another state or federal jurisdiction

rules.title: C-23 Ornamental Metal scope

rules.title: C-27 Landscaping scope
rules.plain_english: C-27 contractors construct, maintain, repair, install, or subcontract landscape systems and facilities for gardens and grounds, and prepare and grade land for architectural, horticultural and decorative treatment.

public and private gardens and grounds
preparing and grading plots for architectural, horticultural and decorative treatment
